subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm aiming for a compact but detailed module, around 400 lines, focused on getting the API usage right. I'm picturing a Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith: stocky build, big pauldrons, braided beard, hammer raised, with an anvil and glowing iron in front of him.

Now I'm working out the skeleton geometry: hip root height, spine chain through hips/chest/neck, arm positions with the hammer angled down in the right hand, legs with knee bends, and anvil placement in front of the figure. I'm being careful to define the root joint correctly before building out the limb and spine chains.

Defining torso loft stations...

Now planning the head and face: a bulbous nose, heavy brows, an iron open helmet with small horns, and a thick braided red-orange beard built from loft or extruded blade shapes.

Layering downward-pointing cone spikes gives the beard its chunky texture, while eyes get placed as small spheres positioned using local head coordinates (forward, up, and left/right offsets) relative to the skull center.

For the arms, I'm setting up shoulder-elbow-wrist chains with mirrored positions for left/right sides, angling them outward and slightly forward-down for a natural rest pose, with the right arm positioned to eventually hold the hammer.

Still defining the arm geometry...

Still working out hammer geometry...

Now positioning the left hand with tongs gripping the glowing iron bar against the anvil, adjusting wrist coordinates and anvil dimensions so both hands can plausibly reach their tools from the raised hammer position to the anvil surface.

Defining chain joints and arms...

Checking hip-to-ankle distance against leg segment lengths to confirm the bend works, then adding a darker toe cap. Now I'm designing torso wear: a leather apron over the belly, a belt with brass buckle, and shoulder pauldrons made from scaled half-spheres with brass rivets and a spike on top, riding on the chest bone near the shoulder joint. Setting up the color palette starting with skin tone.

Going with a Warcraft-style blue dwarf tunic, orange-red beard, brown apron, and a metal palette of iron, dark iron, and brass with gold trim, plus glowing hot-iron and ember tones for the forge bar and a few small glowing spheres as sparks. I'm constructing the anvil from boxes for the base, waist, and top face, a cone for the horn, and a step, positioned so it stands on a log stump.

Working out the stump and anvil dimensions...

Now I'm shaping the helmet dome with a lathed profile curve, adding a brass torus band oriented horizontally around the head, and starting on the horn spikes as curved extrusions attached to the head bone.

For the face, I'm building a scaled skull sphere with cheek spheres, a reddish nose sphere positioned forward and up, and heavy orange brow boxes tilted outward on each side to give a fierce expression.

Adding eyes, mustache, and beard geometry...

I'm working out the torso proportions, with the loft depth giving shoulder width and chest depth, plus a belly sphere to bulk out the tunic. Then I'm positioning an apron panel extruded from a flat outline, placing it against the front of the torso near the belly.

I'm shaping the apron outline as a trapezoid-like bib polygon narrowing toward the chest, and deciding which bone to attach it to—leaning toward the hips or chest joint for proper positioning.

Now I'm adding apron details like pockets, stitching, and tool loops, then working out the belt geometry—considering a torus shape around the belly, adjusting its radius, tube thickness, and orientation to fit the torso's elliptical cross-section.

Still working out belt and torso geometry...

I'm skipping detailed pec work and moving to the shoulder yoke, planning dwarf-style pauldrons using a scaled half-sphere with a brass trim torus at the shoulder joint, plus a short neck spike. I'm setting up the arm's joint chain from shoulder through elbow to wrist, parented to the chest joint, and defining the torso loft top near the neck for a short sweeping transition.

Now I'm working through the hands: a fist sphere at the wrist, with a palm box and four curled finger capsules plus a thumb wrapping around the weapon handle, computing hand orientation from the elbow-to-wrist direction so the fingers curl naturally.

Now I'm working out hand-tool attachment points: positioning the hammer handle through the right fist with a simple sphere for the gripping hand, then setting up the left hand gripping the tongs with two rod jaws meeting at a pinch point along the bar.

I'm figuring out the bar's dimensions and placement relative to the top plate so they don't clip, and setting up a gradient glow for the bar with a hot white tip at one end fading to orange.

Now I'm adding scattered glowing spark cubes above the bar, then moving on to character details: brass-buckled boot cuffs, dark leather pants, a blue tunic with gold trim, and an iron bracer wrapping the forearm using a tapered sweep along the arm.

I'm defining a shared taper function for the arm and bracer radii, adding a rolled sleeve cuff ring near the elbow, and now working out beard braids on each side of the chin as curved sweeps with small brass ring bands spaced along them, figuring out the right orientation axis for each ring.

For the mustache, I'm building symmetric curl sweeps outward from under the nose using head-relative coordinates, checking that the coordinate syntax supports left/right offsets properly.

I'm defining a helper function to shorthand head-local positioning, then working out the geometry for brow ridge and eye placement—computing where the eye sockets intersect the skull sphere's surface using the radius and lateral offset to find the correct forward depth.

Now I'm sizing up the skull radius, positioning the nose with its own protrusion depth, and planning the mustache placement around it. For the beard, I'm layering multiple scaled spheres at decreasing heights to build bulk, then adding downward-pointing spike clusters for the tapered beard tip.

I'm also working out the jaw structure since the mouth will be hidden beneath the beard mass—attaching the lower beard bulk to a separate jaw bone so it articulates, coloring the spikes with a root-to-tip gradient from dark rust to orange, and adding a small dark slot to suggest the mouth opening.

Then I'm setting up the joint chain for the head: establishing the jaw joint anchored at the head with an aim direction toward the chin, then building the neck and head joints off the chest so the whole upper skeleton connects properly.

Now I'm defining the spine chain itself — a three-point catmull curve from hips through mid-spine up to the chest, naming each segment spine1, spine2, and chest, with chest becoming the tip of this chain for later limb attachments. The hips joint also gets tagged with a spine role, and I'm setting up the leg chains parented to the hips with hip, knee, and ankle joints, feeding in the limb's computed points as the path.

For clothing layers, I'm working out whether to loft the torso as a single tunic shape or split it into separate pants and tunic pieces — deciding to use a sphere for the pants region around the hips and a loft for the tunic above it, overlapping enough that a belt can hide the seam, and considering a gold trim running down the tunic's front for detail.

Since a chest emblem would get covered by the beard, I'm instead placing a small gold anvil-and-hammer emblem on the apron bib around hip height, extruding a simple anvil silhouette outline there as a dwarven craftsman detail.

Writing extrude parameters...

Now I'm designing the hammer itself: a wooden handle with leather wrap bands and pommel, an iron head with brass striking faces on each end and a faint glowing rune box for magical flair. I'm positioning the striking faces along the head's local x-axis (roughly world X), offset slightly from center, with the handle tilting toward +z while keeping x fixed.

For the rune glow, I'm computing an offset along the head's tilted local axes so it sits just beyond the front face depth, aligning it with the same aim direction used for the handle tilt to keep everything consistent.

Writing helper functions...

Placing rivets around the pauldron rim...

Now I'm planning boots with pants cuffs tucked in, then moving to write the actual code. I want to keep the part budget around 150-200 and set up color constants first, importing the builder utilities and glow kit. I'm also considering using the metal paint helpers for iron and brass surfaces—like the anvil, hammer head, and pauldron trim—keeping in mind that glow effects won't work on painted parts, so I need to choose carefully which pieces get which treatment.

Writing build function skeleton...

Still adding boot geometry...

I'm naming the chain segments for each arm—upper arm, forearm, and hand—and deciding to use catmull interpolation for smooth curves rather than straight polylines. For the arm sweep I'm defining a radius that tapers slightly toward the elbow, with a texture band shift from tunic to skin material, and considering adding a bracer cuff near the wrist with a slightly thicker iron radius.

Adding bracer ridge bands, fists, and fingers...

Since the beard covers the neck area anyway, I'll skip hair details and just add small side sideburn spikes with orange coloring near the ears, plus tiny skin-toned ear spheres at the sides of the head. For the helmet, I'm lathing a profile shape around the head's vertical axis, positioning it at the skull center to create the rounded dwarf helmet silhouette.

Checking clearances: the skull radius shrinks with height, so I need the helmet dome radius to stay larger than the skull surface at every height to properly clear it, while making sure the helmet rim doesn't collide with the brow ridge poking forward at eye level.

I'll raise the helmet base to up 0.14 so it sits above the brow, giving total head+helmet height around 1.3-1.35 and overall figure height near 1.42-1.45, which is reasonable for a stylized stocky dwarf. Now I'm placing the brass rim torus at the helmet base and adding a thin nose guard box extending down from the front of the helmet.

Adding the crest ridge and horn geometry...

Adding a glowing ruby gem, then thinking through beard and jaw shapes—I'm sketching a helper function for creating scaled ellipsoid parts so I can place the lower jaw and beard mass with proper semi-axis proportions relative to the head.

Adding beard spikes in rows...

Now I'm working out the braids hanging from the beard sides down toward the chest, with bead rings and a tassel spike at the end, but I'm noticing the braid placement overlaps with the belly geometry so I need to shorten them to avoid embedding into the body.

Checking the overlap, I decide the beard tip resting against the chest/belly actually looks natural, so I'll stop worrying about perfect clearance and finalize the positions as is. Moving on to the eyes, I'll place small dark pupil spheres slightly forward of the main eye position.

Now I'm working out the stump, tongs, and anvil details — sizing the wood stump cylinder, adding iron hoop bands using thin toruses, and applying a wood grain texture via the grain helper. Then I start thinking about how the dwarf and anvil will stand on the floor.

Adding a belt pouch and anvil emblem details...

I'm embedding the emblem near the bib region and reconsidering the apron geometry so it doesn't float awkwardly against the belly curve—maybe adding leather strap rods connecting the apron corners up to the neck and shoulders for support. Now I'm starting to define the belt as a lathed shape, sketching its outline coordinates.

Adjusting belt radius and z-offset so it clears the apron front without poking too far past the torso in back...

Now designing the belt buckle as a brass box with a darker inset, plus a row of brass studs along the belt front, then setting up the torso loft stations with widths and depths at each height to keep the shoulders wide enough to cover the arm attachment points. I'm deciding to skip adding a backpack or cape for now.

For finishing touches, I'm generating small spark/ember boxes scattered near the forge area with varying glow colors, importing the glow helper, and assigning paints—steel for the hammer head and helmet with slight tarnish, steel for pauldrons, and a flat brass tone for buckle and studs. Now writing the rod sweep code for the tongs...

Still writing geometry code...

I clarify that "aim" corresponds to a Direction parameter, so I should use "dir" instead in the part calls. I'm sketching a torus-ring helper function for circular elements like tongs or bands, and planning the handL bone rods and forearm positioning for the tongs reaching toward the bar.

Now I'm setting up the arm coordinates for both limbs (shoulder, elbow, wrist positions) and computing the hand direction vector from elbow to wrist, then starting to define the hammer's transform.

Next I'm working out the tongs geometry: positioning the fist grip point along the hand direction, placing the handle rods, and calculating the jaw endpoints that pinch around the bar, offsetting the rod pairs by half the bar's thickness.

I'm also figuring out the pivot rivet position at the jaw midpoint, then setting up the bar's hot segment with its glowing orange core and whiter tip color near one end.

Now dividing the bar into three temperature zones—bright yellow-orange near the tip, deep orange in the middle, and darker cooling red-brown toward the grip, placing the tong grip within that cooler zone. I'm noting the anvil's horn position and steel plate coloring, then preparing to write the full scene at around 350 lines.
